<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. IX.|ACCORDING TO S. IOHN.|247}}</noinclude>said, I beleeue Lord. And falling dovvne he adored him.⊣ {{verse|chapter=9|verse=39}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, For iudgement came I into this vvorld: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ By this we see that this miracle was not onely maruelous and beneficial to the blinde, but also significatiue of taking away spiritual blindnesse.}}∷ that they that see not, may see: and they that see, may become blinde. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=40}}† And certaine of the Pharisees that vvere vvith him, heard: and they said to him, VVhy, are vve also blinde? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=41}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them, If you vvere blinde, you should not haue sinne. but novv you say, That vve see. Your sinne remaineth.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. IX.}}}}

''6. Made clay.''] Christ that could haue cured this man by his onely wil or word, yet vsed certaine creatures as his instruments in working, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=External ceremonies.}}and diuers circumstances and ceremonies, clay, water, anoynting, washing, &c. No maruel then that he and his Church vse such diuersities of Sacraments and ceremonies external in curing our soules.

''22. Put out of the Synagogue.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Heretical translation.}}The Heretikes vntruely translate here (& v. 35.) ''Excommunicate'': to make the simple conceaue the Churches Excommunication to be no other, or no better, or no more rightly vsed against them, then this casting out of the Synagogue of such as confessed our Sauiour. They might as wel haue translated for Synagogue, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Casting out of the Synagogue.}}Church: for the Old Testament, the new: for Law, grace: for flesh, spirit: for Moyses, Christ. For no lesse difference is there betwene, casting out of the Synagogue, and, Excommunication. Besides that, not euery one which was not of the Iewes Synagogue, was therfore out of the communion of the Faithful, many true beleeuers being in other partes of the world not subiect to the Iewes Synagogue, Law, nor Sacraments. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=See in the ''Annot. Mat. 18, 17''.}}And therfore it was not al one to be out of the Synagogue, and to be excommunicated. as now, whosoeuer is out of the Churches communion, either by his owne wil, or for his iust deserts thrust out of it by the spiritual Magistrate, he is quite abandoned out of al the societie of Saincts in heauen and earth, so long as he so continueth. As for the cause of thrusting this poore man and such other out of the Synagogue, and excommunicating Heretikes, there is as great oddes as betwixt heauen and hel: he being vsed so for folowing Christ and his Church, these for forsaking Christ and his Church. Some more agreement there is betwene that corrupt sentence of the Iewes against the folowers of Christ, and the pretended excommunication executed against Catholike men by our Heretikes. although in truth there is no great resemblance. For, the Iewes though they abused their power sometimes, yet had they authoritie in deed by Gods law so to punish contemners of their Law, & therfore it was feared and respected euen of good men. But the excommunication vsed by heretikes against Catholikes or any offenders, is not to be respected at al, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Heretikes ridiculous Excommunication.}}being no more but a ridiculous vsurpation of the Churches right and fashion of the same. for, out of their Synagogues al faithful men ought to flee, and not tarie to be thrust out: according to the warning giuen against Coré and Dathan. ''Be ye separated from their tabernacles, lest you be vvrapped in their sinnes''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Num. 16''.}}<noinclude>{{rh|||Amen,}}</noinclude>
